# Page 21^page=21
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 21 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS Union Minister Giriraj Singh Releases Report ‘Market for Textiles & Clothing: National Household Survey 2024’ On April 6 2026, Union Minister Giriraj Singh, Ministry of Textiles (MoT), released a study report on Domestic Demand of Textiles titled “Market for Textiles and Clothing: National Household Survey 2024” in presence of Neelam Shami Rao, Secretary, MoT, in New Delhi, Delhi. • The survey, conducted by the Textiles Committee, evaluates household demand for Textiles and Apparel (T&A) and serves as a key reference for policymakers and industry to plan growth strategies. Exam Hint: ✓ What? Release of study report on Domestic Demand of Textiles ✓ Name of Report: “Market for Textiles and Clothing: National Household Survey 2024” ✓ Released by: Union Minister Giriraj Singh, MoT ✓ Conducted by: Textiles Committee ✓ Focus: Household demand for Textiles & Apparel (T&A) ✓ Market Size (2024): Rs.14.95 lakh crore ✓ CAGR (2010–2024): 8.3% ✓ Household Demand: Rs.8.77 lakh crore ✓ Per Capita Demand: Rs.6,066 ✓ Fiber Share: MMF & Blends (52.2%); Cotton – 41.2% ✓ Women share: 55.5%. Key Findings of the Report: Market Expansion: The domestic demand for textiles grew from Rs 4.89 lakh crore in 2010 to Rs 14.95 lakh crore in 2024, recording a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 8.3%. Household Contribution: Household demand specifically rose from Rs 4.18 lakh crore (2010) to Rs 8.77 lakh crore (2024). Per Capita Demand: Reflecting rising incomes, the per capita demand for textiles increased from Rs 2,119 in 2010 to Rs 6,066 in 2024 (7.8% CAGR). Fiber Preferences: • Man-Made Fibre (MMF) & Blends: Account for the largest share at 52.2% (Market value: Rs 4.47 lakh crore). • Cotton: Remains the second most important fiber at 41.2% (Market value: Rs 3.53 lakh crore). • Silk & Wool: Contribute 5.2% and 1.3% respectively. Textile Market Highlights (2024): Category Value(in Rs) Market Size of Textiles 14.95 lakh crores Domestic Market Size 12.02 lakh crores Household Demand 8.77 lakh crores Per Capita Demand 6,066

# Page 22^page=22
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 22 Daily Content PDF Consumption Patterns and Consumer Trends: Gender-wise Demand: Women are the primary drivers of textile consumption, accounting for 55.5% of purchases, compared to 44.5% by men. Product Popularity: • Men: Jeans emerged as the fastest-growing category. • Women: Leggings gained significant prominence. • Traditional Wear: Items like sarees, dhotis, and salwar kameez remain staples in the domestic market. Sustainability & Technical Textiles Trends: Sustainability Hub: The total demand for sustainable textiles (recycled, reused, and reprocessed) reached Rs 37,000 crore in 2024. • Reused and retailored products account for 58% of this segment. Technical Textiles: There is a significant surge in the adoption of technical textiles such as masks, sanitary napkins, diapers, and surgical disposables. Rural & Urban: Interestingly, rural households account for nearly 58% of technical textile consumption, while urban areas contribute 42%. About India’s Textile Industry: Economic Contribution: India’s textile sector contributes around 2% to Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and about 11% to manufacturing Gross Value Added (GVA). • Additionally, the sector is the second-largest employment generator in the country. • For Financial Year 2026–27 (FY27), the MoT has been allocated Rs.5,279.01 crore in the Union Budget. Export Performance: It is the 6th largest exporter of T&A globally, with the United States of America (USA) and European Union (EU) together accounting for nearly 47% of exports. Global Production Leadership: India is the world’s second-largest producer of cotton (23.83% of global output), with production expected to reach 7.2 million tonnes by 2030. It is also the largest producer of jute and the second-largest producer of man-made fibres (MMF), including polyester, viscose, nylon, and acrylic. Market Outlook: India’s textile and apparel market is projected to reach USD 350 billion by 2030. About Ministry of Textiles (MoT): Union Minister- Giriraj Singh (Constituency- Begusarai, Bihar) Minister of State (MoS)- Pabitra Margherita (Rajya Sabha- Assam) NSO Launches Inaugural Annual Survey of Incorporated Services Sector Enterprises In April 2026, the National Statistics Office (NSO), under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), officially launched the inaugural Annual Survey of Incorporated Services Sector Enterprises (ASISSE) aimed to develop a comprehensive database of the incorporated (registered) services sector in India. • The newly launched survey, rolled out from April 2026, covers incorporated services sector enterprises across all States and Union Territories (UTs), with the reference period being the Financial Year 2024-25 (FY25). Exam Hints: ✓ What? Release of the Inaugural edition of ASISSE ✓ Released by: NSO, MoSPI ✓ Reference Period: FY25

# Page 23^page=23
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 23 Daily Content PDF ✓ Purpose: To develop a comprehensive database of the incorporated services sector in India ✓ Eligible Entities: Registered under the Companies Act, 1956/2013 or LLP Act, 2008 ✓ Focus Sectors: Trade, Transport, Hospitality, IT, Education and healthcare ✓ Expected Enterprises: Nearly 1.21 lakh enterprises ✓ Source for Survey: GSTN Database About ASISSE: Target Enterprises: The survey covers corporate entities in the services sector, which are registered under the Companies Act, 1956/2013 or Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) Act, 2008. Services Sectors Covered: The new survey covers a wide range of services sectors which include: trade, transport, hospitality, Information Technology (IT), education, healthcare, among others. Methodology: The ASISSE survey is expected to cover nearly 1.21 lakh enterprises, using the Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN) database. Legal Provisions: As per NSO, the survey will be conducted under the provisions of Collection of Statistics (Amendment) Act, 2017, and through the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023 and data will be collected through a secure web-based portal. Key Highlights: Release of Explainer: The NSO also released a reader-friendly explainer on the survey titled “Know Your Survey: A User Guide to the Annual Survey of Incorporated Services Sector Enterprises (ASISSE)”, explaining the key aspects of the survey in a simple and structured manner for the participating enterprises as well as for the general public. Significance: With launch of ASISSE, the Government of India (GoI) will now have 3 surveys: Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) that captures data on the registered manufacturing sector and the Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE) that surveys unincorporated segments. • Together, these surveys will generate a comprehensive framework for the non-agricultural sector. About National Statistics Office (NSO): Background: It was established on 23 May 2019 by merging the Central Statistics Office (CSO) and the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) to streamline statistical activities. Function: It is mainly responsible for the collection, compilation, and dissemination of official statistics. Chief Statistician of India (CSI) – Dr. Saurabh Garg (Secretary of MoSPI) Headquarters– New Delhi, Delhi GoI Notifies Amaravati now sole capital of Andhra Pradesh In April 2026, the Ministry of Law & Justice (MoL&J) formally notified Amaravati as the exclusive capital of Andhra Pradesh (AP) after both houses of Parliament i.e. Lok Sabha (Lower House) and Rajya Sabha (Upper House), passed Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 and received presidential assent. • With passage of the Amendment Act and President’s assent, Amaravati will now be the permanent capital city of AP. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Notification declaring Amaravati as Sole Capital of AP ✓ Notification Issued by: MoL&J

# Page 24^page=24
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 24 Daily Content PDF ✓ Declared under: AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 ✓ Retrospective Effect: From June 02, 2024 ✓ Key Amendment: Section 5 of APR Act, 2014 Key Details: Effective From: As per the official notification, the newly enacted Amendment Act, shall be deemed to have come into force on June 02, 2024. Key Changes: The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026, amended the Section 5 of AP Reorganisation (APR Act, 2014) which stated that Hyderabad would remain the common capital of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh for 10 years. • Also, by inserting the word “Amaravati” into the APR Act, 2014, it nullifies the decision of previous AP government which proposed 3 capitals for the state – Amaravati, the legislative capital; Visakhapatnam, the executive capital; and Kurnool, the judicial capital. Constitutional Provisions: Article 2 and Article 3 of the Constitution of India confer exclusive powers upon Parliament to form or establish or completely alter and destroy the identity of the existing states. • Article 1 of the Constitution states that it is within the exclusive domain of Parliament to form any state, set boundaries, and name a state in the Union. • Also, Articles 2, Article 3 and Article 4 of the Constitution specifies that the power to establish a state’s capital is inherent to, and inseparable from, the power conferred upon Parliament. About Andhra Pradesh (AP): Chief Minister (CM) – Nara Chandrababu Naidu Governor- Justice (Retired) S. Abdul Nazeer Capital- Amaravati National Parks (NPs)- Rajiv Gandhi (Rameswaram) NP, Papikonda NP India’s Indigenously Built Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor at Kalpakkam, TN Achieves Criticality On April 6, 2026, India’s 1st indigenously developed 500 Megawatt electric (MWe) Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam in Tamil Nadu (TN), successfully achieved first criticality, marking the start of a controlled nuclear fission chain reaction. • This achievement will give a significant boost to the crucial second stage of India’s 3-stage nuclear programme. Exam Hints: ✓ What? India’s 1st indigenously built 500 MWe PFBR achieved criticality ✓ Location: Kalpakkam, TN ✓ Significance: Start of controlled nuclear fission; boost to 2nd stage of nuclear programme ✓ Fuel Type: Uranium-Plutonium Mixed Oxide (MOX) fuel ✓ Designed by: IGCAR ✓ Developed by: BHAVINI. About PFBR: Type of Breeder: It is a sodium-cooled, pool-type Fast Breeder Reactor (FBR) that produces more fuel than it consumes. Designed by: It was designed by the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR), a Research & Development (R&D) centre under the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE). Developed by: PFBR, developed and operated by Bharatiya Nabhikiya Vidyut Nigam Limited (BHAVINI), a Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE) which works under the DAE. Fuel Used: For the initial phase, FBR will operate using Uranium-Plutonium Mixed Oxide (MOX) fuel. Breeding Process: The core of the reactor is surrounded by a blanket of Uranium-238 and fast neutrons convert these fertile Uranium-238 into fissile fuel.

Indian Army Unveils Technology Roadmap for UAS & Loitering Munitions in Delhi In April 2026, the Indian Army (IA) unveiled the ‘Technology Roadmap for Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) and Loitering Munitions’ to strengthen India’s self-reliant drone ecosystem and enhance modern warfare capabilities. • A 50-page strategic document was released by Lt Gen Rahul R Singh, Deputy Chief of the Army Staff (CoAS) (Capability Development & Sustenance), at Bharat Mandapam, in New Delhi (Delhi). Exam Hints: ✓ What? Launch of Technology Roadmap for UAS & Loitering Munitions ✓ Released by: Rahul R Singh, Deputy CoAS (Capability Development & Sustenance) ✓ Focus: Self-reliant drone ecosystem & modern warfare ✓ Coverage: 30 types; 5 categories; ~80 variants ✓ Categories: Surveillance, Loitering Munitions, Air Defence, Special Role, Logistics ✓ Technology: HALE, MALE, MUM-T, Mother-child configuration, Anti-swarm. About Technology Roadmap: Purpose: It provides long-term clarity on the Indian Army’s UAS requirements and aligns operational needs with technological development, guiding industry, academia, and Research and Development (R&D) investments toward priority areas. Scope: The roadmap covers 30 types of UAS and loitering munitions, translating into nearly 80 variants across diverse operational needs. Categories: It is divided into five segments: Surveillance, Loitering Munitions, Air Defence UAS, Special Role UAS, and Logistics UAS. Technology: It includes High Altitude Long Endurance (HALE), Medium Altitude Long Endurance (MALE), swarm drones, First Person View (FPV) drones, anti-drone systems, Manned-Unmanned Teaming (MUM-T), and ‘mother-child drone’ concepts. India Adds Record 6.05 GW Wind Power in FY26, Surpassing 56 GW Total Capacity In April 2026, the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) announced that India achieved its highest-ever annual wind energy capacity addition of 6.05 Gigawatt (GW) in Financial Year 2025–26 (FY26), marking a major milestone in the Renewable Energy (RE) sector. Exam Hints: ✓ What? India Adds Record 6.05 GW Wind Power in FY26 ✓ Announced by: MNRE ✓ Total wind capacity: Crossed 56 GW ✓ Top states: Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra. ✓ India’s wind potential: 1,164 GW. About India’s Achievement on Wind Energy: Record Growth: The addition surpassed the previous record of 5.5 GW set in FY17 and represents a 46% increase over the 4.15 GW added in FY25. Capacity Milestone: India’s total installed wind power capacity has crossed 56 GW, strengthening its global position and supporting the target of 500 GW non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030. Drivers: Growth is driven by policy clarity, improved transmission via Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS), competitive tariffs, and hybrid projects, supported by concessional customs duty, ISTS waiver till June 2028, Renewable Consumption Obligation (RCO), and technical support from National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE).

AWARDS & RECOGNITIONS UP’s Divya Singh Becomes First Indian Woman to Cycle to Everest Base Camp in 14 Days In April 2026, Divya Singh, a 28-year-old teacher from Gorakhpur (Uttar Pradesh, UP), created history by becoming the first Indian woman and second woman globally, after Tammat Bil Khoar of Bangladesh, to reach Mount Everest Base Camp (EBC) on a bicycle. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Became 1st Indian woman to cycle to Everest Base Camp ✓ Who? Divya Singh (UP) ✓ Duration: 14-day expedition

# Page 28^page=28
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 28 Daily Content PDF ✓ Route: Kathmandu (Nepal) to EBC ✓ Global Rank: 2nd woman globally (after Tammat Bil Khoar, Bangladesh) ✓ Altitude: 5,364 m. About the Expedition: Support & Management: The expedition was flagged off by Gorakhpur district officials and managed by Rustadventure1. Route: The expedition covered Kathmandu (Nepal) to EBC via Saleri, Surke, Phakding, Namche Bazaar, Lobuche, and Gorakshep over 14 days with 10–12 hours of daily cycling. Altitude: She reached a height of 5,364 metres (m) (17,560 feet) above sea level under extreme high- altitude conditions. Challenges: She faced −12°C (degree Celsius) temperatures, high-velocity winds, low oxygen levels, fatigue, and rugged terrain including steep climbs and uneven paths. Effort: In impassable sections, she carried her bicycle on her shoulders and successfully completed the expedition through rigorous self-training with limited resources. Recognition: The achievement gained nationwide appreciation, and brought pride to Gorakhpur, UP while inspiring youth, especially women, towards adventure sports. Note: There are two base camps, South Base Camp in Nepal (popular trekking destination) and North Base Camp in Tibet (China). About Mount Everest: Location: Mount Everest is located in the Himalayas on the border between Nepal and China (Tibet region), is known as Sagarmatha in Nepal and Chomolungma in Tibet. Naming: The mountain is named after Sir George Everest, the former Surveyor General of India. Height: It is the highest mountain on Earth at 8,848.86 metres(m) (29,031.7 feet) above sea level. Formation: It was formed due to the collision of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates. # Page 29^page=29
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 29 Daily Content PDF IMPORTANT DAYS International Day of Reflection on the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda 2026- April 7 The International Day of Reflection on the 1994 Genocide Against the Tutsi in Rwanda is observed annually on 7 April to honor over 1 million victims of the 100-day genocide, while also recognizing the suffering of Hutus and others who opposed it. • April 7 2026, marked its 32nd anniversary. Exam Hint: ✓ What? International Day of Reflection on the 1994 Genocide Against the Tutsi in Rwanda ✓ When? April 7 ✓ 2026 Mark: 32nd Anniversary ✓ First Observance: 7 April 2004 ✓ 2026 Event: UN Commemoration at UNHQ, New York (USA). Background: UN Designation: The United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) designated 7 April as the International Day of Reflection on the Genocide in Rwanda through Resolution A/RES/58/234 on 23 December 2003. First Observance: The inaugural observance was held on 7 April 2004, marking the 10th anniversary of the genocide. Title Revision: On 26 January 2018, the UNGA amended the title to ‘International Day of Reflection on the 1994 Genocide Against the Tutsi in Rwanda’ via Resolution A/72/L.31 to explicitly recognize the Tutsi as the primary victims. Alignment: On 20 April 2020, Resolution A/RES/74/273 reaffirmed the title and aligned the UN’s outreach programme with the historical context of the genocide. About 1994 Rwandan Genocide: Duration: The genocide lasted from 7 April to 15 July 1994, spanning 100 days. Victims: Over 1 million Tutsis were killed by Hutu extremists, along with moderate Hutus and opposition figures.
